newsitem.title: USA: ADM seen taking charge for settlement.
newsitem.headline: ADM seen taking charge for settlement.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co might take a charge against earnings, perhaps as early as its fiscal 1997 first quarter just ended, to cover costs of a settlement with the Justice Department, analysts said.

"I assume that is the case. It seems to be an end-all" to a four year investigation into alleged price fixing in the food additives business, said analyst George Dahlman at Piper Jaffray. "It may even be an amendment into this quarter," he said.
ADM was not immediately available to comment on a possible charge against earnings to cover the settlement.

ADM said Monday it agreed to plead guilty to federal charges related to price-fixing and pay fines totalling $100 million. ADM said the agreement, which is subject to court approval, settles the Justice Department's investigation of price-fixing of feed additive lysine and citric acid, and closes a third investigation related to high-fructose corn syrup.

Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum analyst Lou Ehrenkrantz said he does not expect ADM's stock to react negatively to a charge against earnings if one is taken. "People have been waiting for this shoe to fall so long that the price of the stock indicates a sigh of relief," he said.
ADM shares added 1-1/8 to 21-3/4 on turnover of more than 2.6 million shares.

"The market has assimilated the whole story and there are no surprises there," said Ehrenkrantz who has been following the agribusiness giant for five years and maintains a strong buy rating on its shares.
"ADM is once again a very credible story," he said. "You're going to see a resumption in the stock price. It will make up for lost time," he said.
